Korean-themed Warframe 'Narin' Wears a Gat and Dances with Ice Blades
items.summary: It has been a genuinely long time since I last launched 'Warframe'.I believe the last time I played intensely was before the pandemic, but due to the nature of my job, I couldn't stick with one game for long.
items.content:
Not an All-Rounder, but Excels in AoE Offensive Capability

Korean (한국어) KO Add us on It has been a genuinely long time since I last launched 'Warframe'.

I believe the last time I played intensely was before the pandemic, but due to the nature of my job, I couldn't stick with one game for long. Warframe is the kind of game that becomes more enjoyable the more time you invest in it. As much as I wanted to keep playing, playing various games is the destiny of a gaming journalist. Ultimately, despite having logged hundreds of hours into it, Warframe remained dormant in my library for quite a while.

Then, news of a new update arrived: 'Narin's Ice Blade'. While adding new Warframes is nothing unusual for the game, this Warframe was cut from a different cloth. An ability named Hakchum? A skin named Baridegi? What is this?

As you might notice, 'Narin' is the first Korean-themed Warframe. Given that Korea's image in the West is heavily tied to K-pop, I wondered if a Korean-themed frame would be music-focused like 'Octavia' or 'Temple'. Instead, we got a Cold-elemental Warframe wearing a gat and brandishing a rapier. Driven by curiosity alone, I had to try her out myself.

An Offensive Cold-Elemental Warframe Different from Frost

The quintessential Cold-themed frame in Warframe is undoubtedly 'Frost'. Released early in the game's service, Frost is tailored for defense, fulfilling the class fantasy of freezing and locking down enemies. However, 'Narin' takes a somewhat different approach. While Frost is a master of area control and denial, Narin dives into groups of enemies, instantly shutting down their movement, enduring incoming attacks, and wiping them out. Where Frost waits for enemies to approach, Narin takes the initiative and charges in.

Narin's ability kit is built around this exact concept.

Her first ability, 'Neote', lunges forward with her rapier and unleashes numerous ice orbs in front of her. While its raw damage isn't bad, the true value of this ability lies in rapidly stacking 'Ice' across multiple enemies rather than raw damage output. Since it has no particular cooldown, it's an ability you can freely spam whenever you see a crowd of enemies.

Her second ability, 'Naraemagi', absorbs Cold Status Effects from surrounding frozen enemies to restore Shields, granting Overguard if Shields are already at maximum. Since most of Narin's attacks freeze enemies solid, her survivability isn't bad to begin with, but Naraemagi provides a massive boost to her endurance. Even with minimal survivability modding, Naraemagi allows her to stay alive in most situations.

Her third ability, 'Hakchum', spreads ice wings upon cast and grants a floating effect. Players can adjust her altitude using the Spacebar and Control keys. Once positioned, clicking causes her to slam down, creating a wide Cold zone that applies not only Cold Status Effects but also a Cold Damage Vulnerability debuff. Hakchum boasts a fairly long duration, making it effective for defensive lockdown over an extended period. Because it continuously inflicts Cold status, it can also be paired with 'Naraemagi' as a panic button for survival.

Her ultimate ability, 'Nurinarim', is a visually stunning skill whose viability was revived through a recent hotfix. Once you fully fill your Ice meter using other abilities, Nurinarim becomes active. Upon activation, Narin performs an endless dance while a vast Cold area activates around her, dealing continuous damage to nearby foes. During this, she can launch powerful ice blade waves at enemies, which consume her Ice gauge by default—though the consumption rate is reduced based on enemy Cold Status stacks.

While the hotfix greatly enhanced Nurinarim's usability, its initial launch specifications were somewhat awkward, as blade waves could only be launched at enemies marked by Nurinarim. In most combat scenarios, when Narin activated her ultimate and began dealing AoE Cold damage, enemies instantly slowed down. Teammates never missed this window. Consequently, most enemies were wiped out before marks could even apply, making it difficult to execute the blade waves for heavy damage. Of course, the Cold Status Effect itself was still a huge asset to teamplay.

Her passive, 'Sangodae', is extraordinarily strong. Killing an enemy grants a 1% chance per Cold status stack on the target to drop a Sangodae pickup. Collecting it grants an additional 50% Cold damage to weapon attacks and abilities for 10 seconds. It's a straightforward, raw 50% damage boost with no catch.

items.title: A "WARFRAME" HALLOWEEN — The Origin System Gets Ready To Celebrate Spooky Season
items.summary: The annual event returns with in-game rewards and sinister surprises.
items.content:
October is here and, for gamers, that means a veritable banquet of Halloween tricks and treats coming to their favourite games. For Digital Extremes’ WARFRAME , a game already touched by eldritch horror and cosmic slashers , this means autumnal hijinx, both familiar and brand-new. If you’re already lugging it out in the Origin System, expect some familiar (and long-absent!) chills. And if not? Well, here’s your excuse to get started, maybe?

Nights of Naberus : What better place to start the festivities than the tumour-and-meat laden world of Deimos, birthplace of The Infestation and home/prison of the dysfunctionally mutated Entrati family. The Entrati clan have implemented new bounties to celebrate the season, with both previous Naberus rewards and brand-new ones available on completion. Currently live.

Hallowed Nightmares: After an eight-year hiatus, WARFRAME’s Halloween-themed tactical event returns to this universe’s Earth. Run the gauntlet of restless and aggressive ghosts as you hunt the pumpkin-headed Juggernaut, Jack O’Naut! Completion of the hunt will earn you appropriately-themed decor and cosmetics for your arsenal. Currently live.

Finally, Baro Ki’Teer, intergalactic merchant of The Void, will be temporarily replaced by his spookier variant , “Scare-O” Ki’Teer! Ki’Teer will again make a series of weekend appearances, offering his usual mods and cosmetics with a new selection of ghoulish goods for your perusal and purchase. Scare-O Ki’Teer sets up shop on an orbital Relay near you, starting Oct. 16 at 9 a.m. ET.

Stay up to date with WARFRAME details and announcements.

items.title: The Icebind feels like "Warframe 2014" in all the best ways, and now you can finally play it
items.content:
After a small delay, Warframe’s highly anticipated six-player mode, Icebind, is live now, and I chatted with Digital Extremes to learn more.

2026 is about to kickstart a new era of Warframe . We're within touching distance of Tau , the spacefaring action game 's colossal update that will take us outside of the Origin system for the first time. We've seen glimpses of the new Chimera Frames, specifically Brysko. And finally, we got View From the Top, one of my favorite Warframe tracks to date. That's easily the most important part.

But before we venture off to systems unknown, Digital Extremes dropped the Iceblade of Narin update , which introduced the titular frame, Narin, the first female Ice frame, and took us on a quick journey back through Warframe 's past. One of the update's main selling points, however, was the six-player Glacial Defiance mode, which got hit with a slight delay, pushing it back by just over a week. Now, however, Glacial Defiance - now renamed The Icebind - has arrived, and I caught up with Community Director Megan Everett to learn more about it.

It's worth stating right off the bat that The Icebind isn't a raid. It isn't a response to the shuttering of Destiny 2, nor is it the return of Warframe's old eight-player Trials. "We've seen the Reddit threads; we've seen the situation," Everett laughs. "The word 'raid' in itself holds a lot of weight within any gaming community; we are definitely not calling these raids."

I ask what the mode's intent is, and how it's different from the instances we see in other online titles. "I would say that a typical raid has that kind of climactic conclusion or build-up to the boss. That's not what this is; that's what our original raids - our Trials - were. The Icebind is really trying to scratch the itch that players have been asking us to. They have asked us for more coordinated, challenging game modes.

"We've been testing it internally, of course, and we've had some really fun moments of coordinating and squadding up, and making sure I've got my Dante, and someone's got Trinity. Again, it's not a raid , but it's giving the Trials vibe because I'm seeing people like 'oh, gotta get my Trinity back out because it's really challenging and I need my healer,' and I was like 'man, this is Warframe 2014. This is crazy!'"

One of the elements of Icebind that has caused some slight friction, however, is that it doesn't use public matchmaking. Instead, players need to find a six-person group to queue up with. If you're part of an established squad, that's fine, but newer players, or those with a more solo-focus, may struggle to get into games.

"We see the conversation around not being able to publicly matchmake, and that you can't do it solo and it has to be six players," Everett says. "We 100% recognize that is going to be a bit of a hurdle, because it's something that Warframe doesn't do. You can publicly matchmake - obviously, the likes of Elite Temporal Archimedia is very restrictive in its loadout, whereas The Icebind isn't. We're trying to take bits and pieces of functionality that we know players like and do something a little different.

"We have to try something new, and it's not going to be for everyone. We recognize that, and we're of course ready to take that feedback when it does launch to players. We do have intentions to make it not six-player mandatory; it'll launch with six players for sure, but we definitely want to have people in smaller squads to be able to do it. But that won't be at launch. We have a lot of ideas and hopes, but it's going to rely a lot on what players think."

I've also seen concerns on the forums regarding The Icebind's loot. At the moment, drops are performance-based, which comes with its own set of concerns. Much like other Warframe missions, Everett clarifies that you'll receive more rewards if you complete side missions and other content, but everyone will still be compensated for completing The Icebind itself.

"If you succeed as a team and do zero of those [additional] challenges, or even if you fail all of those challenges and still succeed at the mission, you're still going to get the reward in the end," she stresses. "It's still pretty tried and true Warframe in that capacity, it's just if you're putting in the effort to squad up and pick your Warframes and your key and all that stuff, then one would hope that you're also coordinating in-game as well to do those challenges if you want those additional rewards."

As for why that decision has been made, Everett clarifies that it's "to address 'griefing' commentary when it comes to mission side objectives. Considering what the mode is asking of you - dedicated squads, six players, very hard content - we need to ensure any potential griefing options are minimal. If we have the power to alleviate some of those player concerns by making the side objectives a part of the success requirements, then we will. The goal is coordination and teamwork!"

Speaking of coordination and teamwork, there's one question on all of our minds: what are the most busted combinations? As TennoCon's designated tribute and one of Warframe's primary experts, I ask Everett what she suggests - or if she suggests anything at all.

"Honestly, it's fuck it we ball," Everett laughs, although she clarifies that you can only pick one of each frame. "You can't have six Wukongs, you can't have six Revenants. We want to invoke a little bit of what Trials did when I would bring my Loki Irritadiating Disarm, we'd have a Trinity healer - kind of that strategy. And we've seen that kind of come back: it's really good to have a Revenant, it's really good to have a Dante - that's usually me. It's really good to have a Trinity.

items.content:
A new challenge arrives atop the Yuvan Peak, Tenno! Rally your squad, ring the Cryobell and overcome the Binds if you can. The Icebind is an experimental new game mode meant to give you the space to push your loadouts and tackle cooperative objectives. Six-player Squads. Level 999+ Enemies. Randomized modifiers known as Binds. Guaranteed Riven Splicer Rewards with bonus Rewards based on Side Objectives. Will you have what it takes to take on The Icebind? Learn more about The Icebind in our guide video below or in the full Dev Workshop.

To play The Icebind, you must have completed the Angels of the Zariman and Whispers in the Walls Quests as well as unlocked Elite Temporal or Deep Archimedea.

items.title: Warframe Previews This Week's New Challenging Mission Mode: The Icebind
October in Warframe
items.summary: As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following e
items.content:
As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following events this month:

EPOCH OPERATION: TAUBOUND

October 15 - November 17 A unique event unlike anything you've experienced to date, Epoch Operation: Taubound offers all eligible Tenno the chance to become a part of Warframe history. If you want to help open up a path to the Tau System, be sure to have your account ready by completing the "Vor's Prize" Quest before October 15. Players looking to pilot their Vessel for the first time can also complete The Hex and The Old Peace in order to access a new, permanent Prologue Quest setting up the Road to Tau. For full event details – including prerequisites and more – click here.

NIGHTS OF NABERUS

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET Spooky season returns to the Origin System during our annual Halloween-inspired event, with Daughter releasing her inventory of new and returning seasonal Customizations in exchange for Mother Tokens. While Baro Ki'Teer will mark the occasion in the same unsettling fashion as last year (IYKYK), we're also mixing it up by bringing back the Hallowed Nightmares Tactical Alert, allowing you to face off against the fearsome Jack O'Naut for even more Naberus treats. For all the harrowing details, check out our Halloween 2026 Events post.

NEW GAME MODE: THE ICEBIND

October 7 Originally intended to ship alongside Iceblade of Narin as "Glacial Defiance," our new 6-player game mode was ultimately delayed to allow for additional development time and renamed to The Icebind. Accessible in-game starting October 7, these challenging, high-level Missions can be played up to three times weekly, allowing you to put your teamwork (and Loadouts) to the test for valuable Rewards. Visit the official Warframe Forums to learn more about the delay, and further details of the game mode itself.

PRINCESS MARGARET CANCER FOUNDATION QUEST

October 1 - October 31 PMCF Quest (formerly Quest to Conquer Cancer) returns for another October full of special Community streams, donation incentives and Conquera Customizations. Join us all month long and help support The Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation light the way towards a world free from the fear of cancer. Visit the Warframe PMCF Quest webpage for more information or donate directly here.

items.title: The Iceblade of Narin in Warframe Was a Disappointment – Opinion
items.summary: The Iceblade of Narin update in Warframe falls short as a final update in 2026 leading into Tau at the end of the year.
items.content:
Okay, what happened here? Because 2026 for Warframe was big on promises and has sadly fallen short in every content drop following The Old Peace. Shadowgrapher fell off the discussion after a couple of days from its launch. In fact, it’s one of the only updates I have not written a dedicated article for due to how lackluster it was and how frustrating the game mode ended up being. Jade Shadows: Constellations revived a bit of my hope. Despite some of the narrative elements just not working out properly (and giving the only 2 protoframes that lacked depth when compared to past iterations). But now we find ourselves in quite a disappointing place with the Iceblade of Narin update that launched almost two weeks ago.

Well, outside of it being another Warframe update with a little bit of everything – a new frame, weapons, skins, etc. there’s not much else holding it together. Sure, we got a rework for Banshee and a way to lock stats on rivens when you reroll them. But when you look at even Shadowgrapher and a promise made during Devstream 197 , this update feels hollow and bitter to me. Especially when I realized this would also be the final update before things leading to Tau start on October 15th.

With all of this out in the open, I need to at least mention that I am aware that the Glacial Defiance game mode, renamed “The Icebind,” is coming in about a week after being delayed ahead of the update’s launch . This is fine, as it is an endgame activity. But not even the exciting concept of The Icebind would be enough to stave off how I feel about a few major problems with the update and how it’s been executed.

As with every major update in Warframe going as far back as Lua’s Prey. Digital Extremes has added a brand new mission with a dedicated currency that alleviated the grind for the frame in that update. You could either get lucky with drops or spend those resources to get what you’re missing. This has been tried and true for years and has worked flawlessly for Digital Extremes. The only time we have not seen this implemented is in big end-of-year expansions like Whispers in the Walls , Warframe: 1999 , and The Old Peace .

Now let’s look at how Narin and her weapons were added to this update. They now share an existing reward pool with everything in the already existing missions in the Zariman Ten-Zero. The only time you get the new currency is from eximus units that have guaranteed chances to spawn, but that’s it. There is no new mission where the warframe and weapons are tied to. This makes it so you now have to fight with low drop chances to maybe get an Aeolak part when you want a blueprint for Narin. Not to mention, I have not seen the new weapon blueprints drop at all. This means you are reliant solely on the new currency.

This is my biggest issue with the update overall. It feels like an overcorrection from Jade Shadows: Constellations, where you could reasonably get everything for Sirius, Orion, Pride, and Wrath within a day or two of casual grind sessions. As of now, I have still not received a blueprint for Narin herself from exterminations or mobile defense. It feels much more luck-reliant to get her blueprints than even Follie, Sirius, or Orion’s parts in the more recent updates.

I feel they could have easily added a new survival or even interception mission and tied the drops there, with entropic eximus units spawning frequently, but they instead chose to inject Narin’s blueprints into an existing drop table and rely on the currency to do the rest of the work. While this is a major disappointment overall, this isn’t even the biggest issue of the update, and that involves what was said in Devstream 197.

During Devstream 197, Creative Director Rebecca Ford stated that the story of the update will be tied to the choice you made during The War Within. It was not explicitly stated as a continuation or anything of the like. But this promise still rubs me the wrong way in how it was handled. That being there was no real integration or narrative elements to the update at all. In fact, I find it strange that Narin exists in the way she does and froze the moment on Yuvan Peak as she did. It just feels off. Especially with all the new Zariman posters everywhere and the console for Melica being there when it wasn’t before. Where did she come from? Why did she freeze that moment in time?

Even if past updates also faltered in warframe introductions, namely Follie at the beginning of the year, they still had some commentary and narration to listen to if you wanted to piece things together. When it comes to Narin, unless The Icebind fixes this? Which I highly doubt it will. Narin will be just another warframe to add to the roster and not much else. This is very disappointing, especially coming off updates like Jade Shadows: Constellations and Shadowgrapher that did this part better.

While Digital Extremes never explicitly stated there would be a quest of any kind, Narin is just going to remain a mystery. With only the explanation in the devstream to give her any narrative coherence to her backstory. But there’s one last part of this update that really bugs me, especially with Tau on the horizon .

I do know that we have the Epoch Operation coming on the 15th , which I will be playing. But with Tau in December (most likely). This might be the last major update for the solar system we can expect for a while. After all, we are heading to a brand new solar system as we take the next major step of the ongoing story, and Digital Extremes will be focused on fleshing Tau out. With this in mind, this initially gave me some level of expectation for Iceblade of Narin . Mentioning The War Within, and going back to the Zariman? It felt like an ominous cliffhanger in the making. But it just did not meet any of those expectations.

Combining everything above, from the lack of a dedicated game mode for the grind for Narin and her weapons. As well as the absence of any narrative coherence or integration for Narin besides what was said in the devstream. The Iceblade of Narin update just missed the mark entirely. It is very disappointing considering just how consistent Digital Extremes has been with these types of updates for years. Even last year’s update around the same time, The Vallis Undermind , had a lot more meat on its bones.

I will still be checking out The Icebind and the Epoch Operation. However, I feel like this update did not live up to the mystery and hype of its reveal. While I do like Narin and her kit (after the recent hotfix), and Nunchasa especially, I feel like there was a lot more that could have been done with this update to prevent it from feeling disappointing.

items.title: Protea Prime and Ivara Prime Enter Prime Resurgence
items.summary: Protea Prime A master of battlefield preparation, Protea Prime brings tactical ingenuity and devastating technology to every mission. Deploy her arsenal, control the flow of combat and keep your squad supplied while turning the battlefield
items.content:
Protea Prime

A master of battlefield preparation, Protea Prime brings tactical ingenuity and devastating technology to every mission. Deploy her arsenal, control the flow of combat and keep your squad supplied while turning the battlefield to your advantage. Protea Prime is a versatile addition to any Arsenal, giving Tenno the tools to adapt to whatever the Origin System throws their way.

Ivara Prime

Stalking from the shadows and waiting for the perfect moment to strike, Ivara Prime is a huntress ready to claim her prey. Ivara Prime draws her bow and disappears into the shadows before striking with deadly precision. With a versatile Quiver, powerful Artemis Bow and the ability to move unseen, Ivara Prime is a natural choice for Tenno who prefer stealth and careful execution.

Prime Warframes

Want to learn more about Prime Warframes? Check out our Guide to Prime Warframes video for a helpful breakdown of what Prime Warframes are, different ways you can earn them and how you can purchase Prime items.

items.content:
With Iceblade of Narin now live, there's lots to see and do at Yuvan Peak and elsewhere aboard the Zariman. But after you've had a chance to explore our latest update, the spooky season beckons… Move from the chilly to the chilling with a look at Warframe's seasonal October content below:

Nights of Naberus

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET Your favorite spine-tingling, seasonal event is back with a bevy of bone-chilling items available from Daughter in exchange for Mother Tokens. Alongside a full inventory of previous offerings, you'll also find some tempting new treats, including:
  • Calaverita Liset Skin
  • Follie Coulrophobia Glyph
  • Voruna Prime Massacre Glyph
  • Sirius vs. Orion Poster
As in years past, Mother Tokens can be obtained by completing Bounties in the Cambion Drift, or by trading additional Resources with Grandmother.

Hallowed Nightmares

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET During the Nights of the Naberus, you'll have the opportunity to take on a Halloween-themed Tactical Alert not seen for several years. Face down the fearsome Jack O'Naut to earn the all-new Jack O’Naut Keychain Sugatra along with:
  • Jack O'Naut Recall Glyph
  • Manic Noggle
  • 50,000 Credits

"Scare-o" Ki'Teer Returns

October 16 @ 9 a.m. ET - November 8 @ 9 a.m. ET The Void Trader's vexing variant will once again make a series of weekend appearances all month long, offering his usual wares along with some beautifully baleful items you haven't seen before! If you enjoyed his unique inventory last time around, you won't want to miss what he's bringing to this year's bizarre bazaar starting at 9 a.m. ET and ending at 9 a.m. ET on the following dates:
  • Visit 1: October 16 - October 18
  • Visit 2: October 23 - October 25
  • Visit 3: October 30 - November 1
  • Visit 4: November 6 - November 8

Tennotober

October 1 @ 12:01 a.m. ET - October 31 @ 11:59 p.m. ET It wouldn't be fall without Tennotober, Warframe's community art challenge supporting the Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation Quest. Find this year's guidelines and prompts on the official Warframe Forums, where you can share your illustrations and Capturas to participate.

Excalibur Nights of Naberus Plushie Giveaway

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - October 9 @ 11 a.m. ET We've collaborated with our friends at Makeship to bring you a delightfully devilish new plushie version of Excalibur. Adorned with the Nyctalus Ephemera and colored for the occasion, the master swordsman looks markedly malevolent yet cuddly as ever. We're giving one away to three lucky Tenno who enter our giveaway via Gleam.

items.title: Iceblade of Narin Official Soundtrack
items.summary: Amid the frigid fanfare of our Iceblade of Narin launch, we're proud to once again deliver Warframe's latest musical tracks to major streaming platforms for your listening enjoyment. The talent, creativity and ingenuity of our remarkable So
items.content:
Amid the frigid fanfare of our Iceblade of Narin launch, we're proud to once again deliver Warframe's latest musical tracks to major streaming platforms for your listening enjoyment. The talent, creativity and ingenuity of our remarkable Sound Team reverberates across the three tracks comprising this release. Drawing inspiration from a traditional Korean musical style called Sanjo, each song evokes the powerful, dynamic movements of a sword dancer — just like our 66th Warframe, Narin. The melodies recorded for Neote's Dance also inspired the vocals in Ice Speaker, which further combines familiar tunes associated with both the Zariman and the Man in the Wall for a unique aural motif befitting the narrative strands threaded through our latest update (as well as the intensity of the upcoming Glacial Defiance game mode).

Where can I listen?

You can find the Iceblade of Narin Official Soundtrack on:
  • Spotify
